A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same EGNN study, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–D. All content can be directly matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments, evaluations on seven benchmarks, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and computational measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons in Tables 2–3 and supplementary results in Tables 7–9.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same spectral-energy transformations, left/right energy gating, GraphSAGE backbone, weighted loss, and time-series extension.

E1.justification: Both versions use Amazon, YelpChi, T-Finance, T-Social, SWaT, WADI, and MSL, together with the same BA and Minnesota graph experiments. No dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding comparisons, including UniGAD among the static baselines and TranAD, USAD, and GDN in Table 3. Appendix computational comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain identical splits, metrics, preprocessing, training budgets, model configurations, temporal windows, strides, and threshold-selection procedures.

E4.justification: The energy-branch, fusion, backbone, and gate ablations in Table 4, window/hop analyses in Figure 5 and Table 7, and spectral-energy and computational analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Run-count and seed descriptions, mean-and-standard-deviation reporting in Table 9, and uncertainty displays in Figure 5 are identical. No statistical reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged, including appendix results. For example, EGNN's T-Social F1-macro remains 95.40 in Table 2, and its SWaT F1-macro remains 86.03 in Table 3.

T1.justification: The graph assumptions, left-shift definition, spectral-energy equations, complexity analysis, and Appendix A derivation are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about detecting camouflaged anomalies, local spectral-energy modeling, temporal extension, scalability, and empirical superiority.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Appendix D retains the same limitations concerning node-attribute anomalies, unweighted and undirected graphs, and dependence on labeled anomalies; the impact statement is also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same hardware, optimizer, hyperparameters, preprocessing, and reproducibility information. The code-access link is unchanged; the added funding acknowledgment supplies no technical implementation detail.

R1.justification: Cited works, bibliography entries, and research positioning remain identical, including Section 5's comparison with spatial, spectral, and temporal approaches.

P1.justification: v2 moves Ahmad Taha before Taylor T. Johnson and removes Taha's middle initial. The acknowledgment adds NSF grant 2619576 and lightly edits the disclaimer. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Small visual changes affect the author line, arXiv margin stamp, and acknowledgment line wrapping. All six figures and nine tables retain identical content, formatting, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 updates author presentation and funding acknowledgment while preserving the scientific argument, empirical evidence, derivations, reproducibility information, and limitations. These administrative and minor presentation edits produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
